newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar stays steady as demand stagnates.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar stays steady as demand stagnates.

text.p: Sugar prices held steady on Tuesday as demand from retail and bulk consumers stagnated even at lower levels, dealers said.
Ready sugar S-30 was steady around 1,425/1,450 rupees per quintal (100 kg). Ready sugar M-30 was offered at 1,460/1,500 rupees per quintal.
In mill delivery, sugar S-30 was quoted at 1,360/1,390 rupees per quintal and M-30 at 1,385/1,415 rupees per quintal.
Dealers said there had hardly been any purchases from bulk consumers such as soft drink manufacturers.
Dealers said they were awaiting the release of free sale sugar quota for the next quarter of July-September.
"If the fresh free sale quota is higher than the previous one at 2.17 million tonnes, then prices may fall further. If it is lower, then prices will recover," said a dealer.
